title: Entitlement slicing and observable synthesis playbook
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a pragmatic design + rollout playbook for splitting large, monolithic permission checks into smaller, observable 'entitlement slices' and producing synthesized evidence bundles suitable for automated SIEM ingestion and compliance queries. The goal: make RBAC v2 checks both more debuggable and easily auditable without blowing up cardinality in logs or creating huge per-request payloads.

Scope:
- Applies to control-plane and management-plane actions (console, API routes that mutate account state, allocation, model lifecycle).
- Out of scope: data-plane token-level content redaction (handled by data access layer).

High-level idea (short):
- Replace single coarse-grained allow/deny with a vector of capability buckets per request. Each bucket is a small capability token (e.g., deploy:can-scale, model:version-edit, billing:invoice-read).
- For each request, produce a compact array of entitlement outcomes (granted/denied/conditional) plus a short provenance fingerprint.
- Synthesize periodic/transactional evidence bundles that aggregate per-request entitlement vectors into a time-windowed artifact. Those bundles are the unit exported to SIEM and to audit queries.

Why this helps (pro/con):
- Pros: enables fine-grained forensics (partial grants, fallback flows), easier canarying of new policies, and smaller per-record size vs dumping full policy text for every check. Evidence bundles compress repeated patterns.
- Cons: needs a compatible telemetry gate and consumer-side parsers in SIEM; initial mapping work to map existing permission names into buckets.

Design details:
1) Entitlement bucket model
- Bucket id: short string, hyphenated, stable (e.g., model:edit, model:deploy, infra:agent-rotate).
- Outcome enum: GRANTED | DENIED | CONDITIONAL (string).
- Reason code: short code (e.g., TTL_EXCEEDED, RATE_LIMITED, ROLE_MISCONFIG).
- TTL/reservation: optional ISO8601 duration when entitlement is reserved (for timebound grants).
- Principal tags: small list of dimension tags (e.g., team:platform, tier:enterprise).

Representation (single-check event example, log-friendly JSON line):
{
  "ts":"2024-10-15T18:03:22Z",
  "request_id":"req_9b1c3f",
  "actor_id":"user:iris.n",
  "actor_type":"human",
  "resource":"org:acme/model:rating-v2",
  "action":"deploy",
  "entitlements":\[
    {"id":"model:deploy","outcome":"GRANTED","reason":"ROLE_MATCH","ttl":null},
    {"id":"infra:reserve-capacity","outcome":"DENIED","reason":"QUOTA_EXCEEDED","ttl":null}
  \],
  "policy_fingerprint":"pf_0a7b3",
  "auth_version":"rbac-v2-a.3"
}

2) Evidence bundle (synthesis)
- Periodic (configurable window: default 10m) or transaction-triggered (e.g., on tenant rollout) aggregation of entitlement events. Produces a compressed artifact: bundle_id, window_start, window_end, principal_summary, top_decision_paths, sampling_rate, checksum.
- Bundle stored in evidence store (immutable), TTL for export, and a pointer exported to SIEM rather than streaming every single entitlement event.

Evidence bundle example (schema sketch):
{
  "bundle_id":"eb_20241015_1800_10m_az1",
  "window":"2024-10-15T18:00:00Z/2024-10-15T18:10:00Z",
  "principal_summary":\[{"principal":"team:platform","count":123}\],
  "top_decisions":\[{"path":"model:deploy->infra:reserve-capacity","count":27}\],
  "sampled_raw_refs":\["req_9b1c3f","req_9b20aa"\],
  "evidence_checksum":"sha256:..."
}

Telemetry contract (fields to add/standardize for SIEM):
- timestamp
- request_id
- actor_id
- actor_type
- tenant_id
- resource (short normalized path)
- action
- entitlement_ids (list of ids)
- entitlement_outcomes (parallel list or array of objects)
- policy_fingerprint
- decision_latency_ms
- decision_node (which machine/policy engine handled it)
- evidence_bundle_id (if aggregated)
- sample_flag (bool)
- exported_by (service name)

Sampling strategy and cardinality control:
- Do NOT emit full entitlement vectors for every read-only request. Only: 1) anomalous outcomes, 2) requests flagged by sampling (default 1%), 3) critical ops (deploy, billing change, key rotation).
- Evidence bundles are the primary unit for long-term SIEM retention; raw entitlement events are short-lived and stored in hot index only for 48–72 hours before being rolled into bundles.

Policy rollout and gating model (phases):
Phase 0 - Mapping (2–3 weeks)
  - Inventory existing coarse permissions -> initial bucket mapping spreadsheet. (Owner: Lina)
  - Small glossary: canonical names, deprecated aliases.
Phase 1 - Pilot + telemetry (2 weeks)
  - Implement entitlement buckets for 5 critical endpoints (console:deploy, api:models.update, billing:read, infra:agent.rotate, keys:create).
  - Start emitting entitlement events to a private telemetry index (no SIEM export).
  - Validate consumption by SRE/observability team.
Phase 2 - Evidence bundles + SIEM adapter (3–4 weeks)
  - Build synthesis job that creates bundles, signs with checksum, exports metadata to SIEM via existing ingestion pipeline.
  - Test with 30-day replay in staging.
Phase 3 - Canary rollout (1–2 weeks)
  - Canary 5% tenants (split by org size) with sampling enabled.
  - Run policy divergence checks vs old system; produce daily drift reports.
Phase 4 - Full rollout + enforcement (ongoing)
  - Flip enforcement flags and enable timebound reservations for workflows that need it. Monitor regressions.

Rollback and safety nets:
- Fast rollback: toggle enforcement to 'log-only' in control plane (central feature flag).
- For high-sev regressions, revert to legacy gate via routing policy in API gateway (pre-existing fallback path).
- Kill switch: per-region enforcement-off flag with immediate global fallback.

Migration checklist (practical):
- [ ] Mapping spreadsheet complete and reviewed by product owners (sheets id: sh_EntitlementMap_v2).
- [ ] Unit tests for every bucket mapping (target 90% endpoint coverage).
- [ ] Telemetry index schema changes applied to staging (index: entitlements-staging).
- [ ] Evidence synthesis job deployed in read-only draft mode to staging and run for 48h.
- [ ] SIEM parsing playbook + saved search created (owner: Samir).
- [ ] Communication (email + #ops) for canary tenants with rollback schedule.
- [ ] Playbook for customers who observe breakage (contact CS + automatic mitigation flow).

Operational metrics to watch:
- Decision latency p50/p95 (target p95 < 20ms additional overhead)
- Number of unique entitlement ids emitted per hour (target: bounded growth < 10% per month)
- Drift ratio: % requests where old-system decision != new-system decision (target < 0.5% before enforcement)
- Evidence bundle generation success rate
- SIEM ingestion success and parsing errors

Open questions / trade-offs (TODOs):
- How to encode cross-tenant delegated grants (service accounts granting ephemeral leases) in the bundle without exposing tenant mappings? (privacy concern).
- Do we let customers opt in to richer principal tags (they will increase cardinality in SIEM)?
- Sampling policy heuristics: weight by anomaly score, actor risk score, and tenant tier. Need a simple MVP.

Notes to self / implementation hints:
- Keep bucket ids short and human-friendly; avoid noisy GUIDs.
- policy_fingerprint should be stable per policy commit (CI job attaches fingerprint).
- Evidence bundle signer: use platform key, rotate monthly.
- For fast prototyping, reuse existing telemetry library (obs-logger) and add a lightweight envelope for entitlements.

Appendix A: quick diffs vs existing RBAC v2 design docs:
- This doc prioritizes synthesis/compression (evidence bundles) as primary export unit to SIEM, rather than streaming everything.
- Emphasizes timebound reservations (TTL) as first-class to support cross-service workflows (deploy -> reserve capacity).

Appendix B: quick sample SIEM ingestion mapping (splunk / cortex-friendly):
- sourcetype: redwood:entitlement:bundle
- fields: bundle_id, window_start, window_end, tenant_id, principal_tags, top_decisions, sampled_raw_refs, checksum
- recommended retention: bundles 365d, raw entitlement events 7d

If you read nothing else: start with the mapping spreadsheet and building the pilot telemetry for the 5 endpoints.
